commands.shell_local: The desktop can keep the unsealed key in its long-lived process cache. A one-shot CLI process would discard that key immediately on exit, so its next mutation prompts normally instead.
commands.equivalence: Process-lifetime credential-store control only; it does not change persisted launcher state.
Create the sealed file after the same confirmation and passphrase decisions without changing the selected backend.
Re-seal the existing file under a replacement passphrase.
Confirmed deletion of the sealed file and all secrets it contains.

commands.shell_local: The desktop can erase a key retained by its long-lived process. The CLI retains no key after any invocation exits, so it is already sealed at that boundary.
commands.equivalence: Process-lifetime credential-store control only; both shells retain no key after their process ends.

commands.shell_local: The desktop needs an IPC reply channel for its ambient prompt; the CLI passphrase source reads the controlling terminal directly, so there is no domain operation or subcommand to mirror.
commands.equivalence: Prompt transport only; core receives the same zeroizing passphrase answer from either shell.
Path-free edit of public account fields.
Edit profile display and launch fields without replacing ownership or paths.

Switch one program off; nothing is deleted. Switching one on needs consent the shell cannot yet ask for, so it is terminal-only.
Confirmed deletion of one write-only secret.
Sweep every stored secret for an account.

Preview core's account-sharing-aware removal plan.

commands.shell_local: The desktop confirmation spans IPC calls and must invalidate its pending capability explicitly; the CLI plans and confirms in one synchronous command and retains nothing when declined.
commands.equivalence: Confirmation-lifetime control only; both shells consume a plan only after confirmation.
Consume a freshly confirmed core removal plan.

commands.shell_local: The desktop asks the operating system to open a current core-issued row id; the terminal renders public rows without owning a window or an ambient browser action.
commands.equivalence: Presentation transport only; the URL is admitted and retained by core rather than accepted from either user interface.

commands.shell_local: The desktop asks its file manager to reveal one closed launcher-owned target; the terminal already prints paths into its controlling terminal and performs no ambient file-manager action.
commands.equivalence: Presentation transport only; every target resolves from current core or process state.

commands.shell_local: The long-lived desktop process retains a bounded diagnostic list for its window; each terminal invocation writes diagnostics directly to its controlling terminal.
commands.equivalence: Process-local presentation diagnostics only.
Publish core's same redacted archive without exposing its bytes or an arbitrary destination path to the webview.

commands.shell_local: The desktop uses a native chooser to mint a process-local folder capability; terminal paths come from argv under the controlling user's direct input.
commands.equivalence: Input transport only; commands consuming the selection still execute through the same core operation.

commands.shell_local: The native desktop binary exposes the same pre-window facts with `apogee --render-report`; apogee-cli has no renderer to inspect.
commands.equivalence: The current native render tier, probe facts, reason, and escalation count.

commands.shell_local: The desktop webview acknowledges that two animation frames rendered; a terminal has no webview process to acknowledge.
commands.equivalence: Renderer-lifetime transport only; it changes no launcher domain record.

commands.shell_local: A person confirms that the desktop window is legible; a terminal does not select or test a graphical renderer.
commands.equivalence: Renderer-lifetime confirmation only; the native probe supplies every reported fact.

commands.shell_local: The desktop owns a close box and may have several concurrent runs to drain; the terminal owns one foreground process and handles interruption directly.
commands.equivalence: Window-lifetime transport only; confirmed shutdown cancels the same core tokens and waits for their streams to end.
